info.description:
Read a workspace's ledger, books, counterparties, milestones, treasury and insights, each payment's evidence and receipt and the monthly close pack, and add counterparties, invoices, milestones and payee links, with a workspace API key.

Every `/api/v1` operation, generated from the OpenAPI document at https://www.vestiarion.xyz/api/v1/openapi.json: one request per operation, in a folder per tag, with its parameters, its body and a saved example of each answer it documents. Optional parameters are listed and switched off; tick one to send it.

**Authentication.** Each request sends `{{apiKey}}` as `Authorization: Bearer`. Import the Vestiarion environment, choose it, and paste a workspace API key as the value of `apiKey`. That value stays on your machine: never share it, and leave the variable's shared value empty. A read-only key reads everything; the `POST` requests need a read-and-write key. No request can approve, reject or pay: no API call can.

New to the API? Start with the "Vestiarion: Getting Started" collection. Guide: https://www.vestiarion.xyz/docs/get-started/postman

exec: throw new Error("apiKey is empty. Choose the Vestiarion environment, top right, and paste a workspace API key as the value of apiKey. That value stays on this machine: never share it.");

request.description:
What this workspace is, and what it can actually do. The first call a client should make: whether payments and yield are live, simulated or unavailable, the workspace clock, running totals, and a description of its configuration. Secrets are never included.

`unavailable` means nothing can pay in this workspace now: its Circle credentials are stored but cannot be read; or it is on Arc mainnet with no Circle account connected yet, or not live yet; or this deployment has Arc mainnet switched off. A cycle refuses to pay then rather than fall back to simulation, so status does not report it as `simulate`. Yield is also `unavailable` on a network with no yield reserve, such as Arc mainnet.

**Key:** any workspace API key; a read-only one is enough.

Reference: https://www.vestiarion.xyz/docs/api/get-status

request.description:
The audit chain, oldest first, as a resumable stream. Because the ledger is append-only and ascending by `seq`, a stored `page.nextCursor` is a watermark: a request from it never returns an entry before it. Persist the last non-null `nextCursor` only after processing every entry in the responses read, and resume from it; the last page, which had no cursor of its own, is returned again, so de-duplicate on `seq`.

`seq` is monotonic within a workspace but not gap-free; continuity is proven by the hash chain, not by `seq`.

**Key:** any workspace API key; a read-only one is enough.

Reference: https://www.vestiarion.xyz/docs/api/list-ledger-entries

request.description:
Replays signatures, body hashes and hash-chain continuity for the workspace the calling key belongs to.

`valid` has three values, not two. `true` verified and `false` broken are findings about the chain; `null` means no verdict was produced, because there was no key to check authorship against. `reason` says which case it is. A key that is stored but cannot be read is a configuration problem, reported in `warnings`, not a finding about the chain.

**Key:** any workspace API key; a read-only one is enough.

Reference: https://www.vestiarion.xyz/docs/api/verify-ledger

request.description:
Adds a payable or a receivable, checked by the rules of the console's invoice form, and recorded in the ledger as `create_invoice` with `via: "api"` and the key's id. It is added as the key's issuer's: if the agent holds it, the issuer cannot approve it, unless they are the workspace's only approver.

The agent decides a payable as one typed in, with every guardrail and the workspace's limits, usually within a minute. The API never approves or pays. A `counterpartyId` the workspace does not hold, including another workspace's, answers `400`.

**Key:** a read-and-write key. A read-only key gets `403 forbidden`.

Reference: https://www.vestiarion.xyz/docs/api/create-invoice

request.description:
Makes a one-time link where a vendor or contractor enters the address they are paid at, recorded in the ledger as `payee_link_created` with `via: "api"` and the key's id. Send `url` to the payee yourself. It is in this answer only, since Vestiarion keeps just its hash, and the answer is sent with `Cache-Control: no-store`. The link works once and expires after 7 days.

The address the payee enters waits for a person in the workspace to confirm it on Counterparties; until then the agent pays nothing to it. Making a link revokes the payee's unused one, so only the newest works. For the same reason this operation keeps no outcome for an `Idempotency-Key`, which would store the link: a repeat makes a new link. A `counterpartyId` the workspace does not hold, or a client's, answers `400`.

**Key:** a read-and-write key. A read-only key gets `403 forbidden`.

Reference: https://www.vestiarion.xyz/docs/api/create-payee-link

Why a payable was paid, or why it is not paid yet, as one signed document: the evidence chain its evidence page shows, from what was agreed to the signatures. Each fact is labelled by how it is known and cites the ledger entries it rests on, and every one of those entries is carried in full with the workspace's public keys, so each can be checked offline with the SDK's `verifyEvidence`. It is the file the page's Download evidence gives, in the format `vestiarion-evidence/1`, with members named by user id, never by email.

A receivable, or an id this workspace does not hold, including another workspace's, answers `404`. Each call reads the transaction on its chain and checks the links people gave, so the evidence reads have a limit of their own per key. Text that came from outside, such as a vendor's name, an invoice number or a memo, is carried as data.

**Key:** any workspace API key; a read-only one is enough.

Reference: https://www.vestiarion.xyz/docs/api/get-invoice-evidence

A receivable, or an id this workspace does not hold, answers `404`.
